name: Badge
summary: Short metadata label or status marker.

a11y.apg: No APG pattern and no role: a badge is a <span> of text, and native semantics are the right answer. Colour is never the only signal — the word inside carries the meaning, so a badge read aloud says the same thing it shows. It is not focusable and has no keyboard interaction; a badge you can click is a Button.

props.name: variant
props.type: neutral | primary | info | success | warning | danger | running | paused | offline | review | red | orange | green | teal | cyan | blue | violet | pink
props.description: Tone of the label. The four operational ones exist because the state of a job is metadata as often as it is a condition; when it is a condition standing on its own, use Status. The eight colour names (red, orange, green, teal, cyan, blue, violet, pink) are CATEGORIES, not states — they mark a group (a section, a type of item) and say nothing about health. They skip yellow, which belongs to the brand, and pass AA in both themes in all three emphases. Pair the colour with a word or a leading icon: colour alone is never the label.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How loud the tone is. `soft` is the tinted pill you already know; `outline` is contour only; `solid` fills with the accent and is what a notification counter wants. All 36 combinations of variant × emphasis × theme were measured for contrast — the lowest is 5.6:1, and the skin spec keeps it that way.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` is the historical size and did not move, so nothing that already uses Badge changed. `xs` (16px, borderless) is the counter that rides on an icon — it is what BottomNav asks for; `sm` sits between them; `lg` is for a standalone label. Every size is its OWN class, never a contextual override: `geometry.spec` holds `.badge` to one height per page, and a rule that shrank it by context reproved — correctly.

props.name: dot
props.description: A status dot before the text, inheriting the current colour. With `anchor` and nothing to show, the dot IS the badge — the plain 8px mark that means "something new".

props.name: leading / trailing
props.description: A glyph before or after the text. They take a NODE, not an icon name, and that is a boundary decision, not laziness: Icon reads the sprite through a hook, so importing it here would drag this module to the client and undo the 118.5 KB that ADR-0026 saved.

props.name: image / imageAlt
props.description: A round picture at the start — an avatar or a flag. Empty alt when it is decorative, which is the usual case beside a name.

props.name: count / max / showZero
props.description: Numeric content. Over `max` it reads `99+`. Zero hides itself unless `showZero`, because an empty inbox does not deserve a mark. `formatBadgeCount(count, max)` is exported so the accessible name can say the same string the eye sees.

props.name: fit
props.description: `content` keeps the badge as wide as its text even inside a column. The default follows the container, and that was measured: `.stack` declares no `align-items`, so a badge inside it stretches (300 px in a 300 px column, 55 px loose in a block). Implemented as `inline-size: fit-content`, not `align-self`, so a badge in a row keeps its vertical centring. Ignored with `anchor`. The native Badge takes the same prop.

props.name: anchor
props.description: Switches to the OVERLAY shape: `children` becomes the thing being decorated (a bell, an avatar, a menu row) and the badge hangs off that corner. Without it, `children` is the pill's content and nothing about the old usage changes.

props.name: anchorShape
props.description: `circle` pulls the badge 14% back into the corner — the `overlap` of one of the references, and the number is theirs, measured in their source. Without it a counter on a round avatar floats off the edge.

props.name: invisible
props.description: Hides the overlay without moving the child. Use it when the count is loading rather than absent.

props.name: children
props.description: The label — or, with `anchor`, the element being decorated. Short by construction: it is a pill, and a badge that wraps to a second line is a sentence in the wrong component.

props.name: badgeContent
props.description: What the overlay shows when it is not a number. Named after a reference library's prop and not `content`, which collides with the HTML attribute of that name.

notes: ANCHORED BADGES ARE aria-hidden, and that is the documented pattern, not an oversight: the count belongs in the accessible name of the thing it decorates — `aria-label="Inbox, 4 unread messages"`. A bell announced as "bell 8" tells nobody what the 8 is.
The cutout ring around an anchored badge defaults to `--background`. Inside a card the surface behind it is `--card`, and CSS cannot guess that — override `--badge-ring` on the container.

NO DISMISS BUTTON, and two independent reasons agree: DIRECTION §3.6 reserves removable classification for `Tag`, and a handler in JSX would force `"use client"` on the pure-markup module. `Tag` does not exist in Aurea yet — a real gap this reading found.
